questions.s: Wrong word form before noun. Use "a constant flow" (adjective) instead of "a constantly flow" (adverb).

questions.q: Select the correct option of the given sentence.
o: Smt. Savithri is the wise than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is wise than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is the wiser than all others in the group.
questions.s:
Answer: Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.

Explanation:
When comparing two or more things, the comparative form "wiser" is used with "than."

  • Wiser is the correct comparative form of wise for comparing.

  • The superlative form is "wisest", which is used with "the" when comparing one among many.

Correct sentence:
"Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group."

Other options are grammatically incorrect.

o: than the one that he had kept
questions.s: Use "comparatively good" or "better", avoid "comparatively better".

questions.q: He is (a) / the most good (b) / player in the team. (c) / No error (d)

questions.q: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.
questions.s:
Correct Answer:true

Explanation:

  • The sentence is: "He is truest to his words."

  • The error lies in the use of "truest", which is a superlative form.

  • In this context, we’re not comparing him with others but simply describing his quality of being faithful or loyal.

  • The correct word should be "true" (adjective), as in:

  • ✅ "He is true to his words."

Let’s eliminate the other options:

  • Most truly – adverbial; doesn't fit the structure.

  • Truer – comparative; not suitable here.

  • Truly – adverb; would modify a verb, not correct here.

Therefore, the correct replacement is true.

questions.s:

questions.q: The second option had lesser impact on the environment compared to the first.
o: lesser impact on the environment
questions.s:
"less" is the appropriate term to compare the impact of the second option with that of the first.

The corrected sentence would be: "The second option had less impact on the environment compared to the first."

  • “Lesser” is used as a comparative adjective before a noun in some formal contexts but is usually used in phrases like “of lesser importance”.

  • When comparing quantities or degree in general, “less” is correct.
